title: Unit – 2 : Session – 10 : SLO – 2 | Dynamic Method Dispatch
sections: Concept: run-time polymorphism (dynamic method dispatch) — an overridden method called through a superclass reference.

Why the subclass method runs: the JVM resolves the call based on the actual OBJECT type (Dog, then Cat), not the reference type (Animal). At run time the object's virtual method table points to the overridden sound(), so Dog.sound() and Cat.sound() execute — this is dynamic binding.
